ev.q: This report describes laboratory-confirmed, breast-feeding--associated transmission of 17DD yellow fever vaccine virus from a recently vaccinated mother
The infant recovered completely, was discharged after 24 days of hospitalization, and has had normal neurodevelopment and growth through age 6 months.

public_health_question.v: Can 17DD yellow fever vaccine virus be transmitted to an infant through breast-feeding after maternal vaccination?

ev.q: This report summarizes the results of that investigation, which determined that the infant acquired yellow fever vaccine virus through breast-feeding.
The Brazilian Committee on Vaccine-Associated Adverse Events classified the child's encephalitis as yellow fever vaccine--associated neurologic disease.
Transmission of Yellow Fever Vaccine Virus Through Breast-Feeding --- Brazil, 2009
The infant, who was exclusively breast-fed, was hospitalized at age 23 days with seizures
a case of meningoencephalitis requiring hospitalization in an infant whose mother recently had received yellow fever vaccine during a postpartum visit.
the investigators reviewed all procedures documented in the medical record performed between the infant's birth and onset of symptoms.
the state health department of Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, was notified by the Cachoeira do Sul municipal health department
the affected infant developed postvaccinal encephalitis requiring hospitalization.
